column1: # Disposition of every CI-reducer abort whose remedy bullets name a `ci_method`
# when a current site carries no row here, or when a row matches no site.
#   sweep  -- the abort is triggered by DEGENERATE DATA, so a bullet naming
#             another ci_method claims that method survives data which has
#             already defeated one. data-raw/sweep-abort-remedies.R measures it.
#   fence  -- the abort is triggered by a design, an argument, or an engine
#             capability, not by the data being degenerate. The named default is
#             not being asked to survive anything, so there is nothing to sweep.

column3: Engine capability: this engine/design pair ships no simulate_refit contract. Nothing about the data is degenerate, so the Monte-Carlo default it names is unaffected.
Data: too few of the parametric-bootstrap refits converged. M93 T1 measured this site 0/90 at the sigma^2 -> 0 boundary and reachable only on degenerate data.
Data: within-subject variance is exactly zero, so the F = MSA/MSE pivot does not exist.
Argument: kappa_m is calibrated per conf_level and not interpolated across levels. The data is untouched by this refusal.
Design: the rater count falls outside the calibrated kappa_m grid.
Design: the subject count falls outside the calibrated kappa_m grid.
Projection: a numeric `unit` whose Spearman-Brown map has passed through its pole. Measured at the M93 implement gate on 28 of 12,600 HEALTHY cells -- the fit is fine, the projection is not.
Data: between- or within-subject variance is exactly zero, so the log F transform and its jackknife SE do not exist.
Data: resampled subjects produced degenerate resamples (SSA = 0 or SE = 0). Stochastic -- a run is evidence about one seed, so the sweep varies seeds as well as geometries.
